title: API 653 Practice Questions 2026: 30 Tank Inspector MCQs with Answers
snippet: 2026 API 653 tank inspector exam prep: 30 practice MCQs with explanations, API 653/650/575/651 references, settlement analysis, NDT, and study tips.
content:
This 2026 question bank prepares candidates for the API 653 Aboveground Storage Tank (AST) Inspector certification. Questions reference API 653 Tank Inspection, Repair, Alteration, and Reconstruction, API 650 Welded Tanks for Oil Storage, API RP 575 Inspection Practices for AST, API RP 577 Welding, API 571 Damage Mechanisms, API RP 651 Cathodic Protection, API RP 652 Linings for Tank Bottoms, and ASME BPVC V and IX.

API 653 Exam Format Overview

  • Closed-book: ~50 questions on basic principles, welding, NDT, corrosion, tank components.
  • Open-book: ~80 questions referencing the API 653 publication package.
  • Total time: 7.5 hours.
  • Pass mark: 70%.
  • Recertification: 3-year reduced, 6-year full cycle.

API 653 Practice Questions

Question 1: Per API 653, the maximum interval between external inspections of an AST is:

  • A. 5 years
  • B. 10 years (or RBI-determined, not to exceed 20)
  • C. 1 year
  • D. Never required

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: API 653 Section 6.3.2.1 requires external inspection at least every 5 years or RBI-determined intervals up to a maximum that depends on shell-thickness measurement intervals and remaining life calculations.

Question 2: The maximum interval for internal inspection of an AST (out-of-service) is:

  • A. 10 years if no corrosion rate is known; otherwise based on bottom remaining life
  • B. 5 years always
  • C. 30 years
  • D. Never required

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: API 653 Section 6.4 limits the internal inspection interval based on bottom corrosion rate and remaining life: not to exceed 20 years; first internal inspection within 10 years for tanks without known corrosion rate; can be extended with RBI per Section 6.4.2.2 to a maximum of 30 years.

Question 3: A typical tank bottom is most susceptible to corrosion:

  • A. Underside from the soil due to moisture and pH
  • B. Top only
  • C. Never
  • D. Only at welds

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: The product side and the underside both corrode, but underside (soil-side) corrosion is often the limiting factor for tank life. API RP 651 (cathodic protection) and API RP 652 (internal linings) are commonly applied to extend bottom life.

Question 4: Per API 653, the minimum thickness for the bottom plate is calculated based on:

  • A. Remaining life, corrosion rate, and protection method
  • B. Tank height only
  • C. Diameter only
  • D. Owner preference

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: API 653 Section 4.4 sets minimum bottom plate thickness based on calculated corrosion rate, projected service interval, and whether the underside has release prevention barrier (RPB), cathodic protection, or lining. Common values 2.5 to 5 mm depending on protection.

Question 5: Tank settlement evaluation per API 653 Annex B compares:

  • A. Measured settlement to allowable uniform, planar tilt, and out-of-plane settlement
  • B. Tank diameter to height
  • C. Wind load to tank weight
  • D. Not evaluated

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: API 653 Annex B provides methods to evaluate settlement: uniform (no shell distress), planar tilt (allowable based on H/D), edge settlement (between shell and bottom), out-of-plane (Fourier analysis to evaluate bending stresses).

Question 6: Per API 653 Section 4.3, the minimum thickness of the shell course is calculated by:

  • A. 1-foot method or variable design point method using current measured thickness less FCA
  • B. ASME VIII formula
  • C. Material specification only
  • D. Owner choice

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: API 653 uses the same 1-foot method (Eq. 4-1) and variable-design-point method (Section 4.3.3.2) as API 650 for required shell thickness, applied with measured thickness less FCA to determine fitness for continued service.

Question 7: A floating roof has potential damage from:

  • A. Seal wear, pontoon leaks, corrosion under sediment, drain hose failure, ice loading
  • B. Only the seal
  • C. No damage possible
  • D. Only welds

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Floating roof external inspection per API 653 includes seals (primary, secondary), pontoon compartments (must be inspected internally), deck plates, drain hoses, anti-rotation devices, and emergency overflow drains. Pontoon flooding causes catastrophic sinking events.

Question 8: Per API 653 Section 9, a major alteration to a tank requires:

  • A. Engineering review, qualified WPS, NDT, and possibly hydrostatic test
  • B. Only welder qualification
  • C. No documentation
  • D. Owner decision only

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: A major alteration (e.g., shell height change, new nozzles in stressed areas, foundation rework) requires engineering review per API 653 Section 9, qualified procedures and welders per ASME IX, NDT per API 650 acceptance criteria, and hydrotest per Section 12.

Question 9: A magnetic flux leakage (MFL) floor scanner is used to:

  • A. Detect bottom plate corrosion and pitting on internal inspection
  • B. Measure shell thickness
  • C. Detect cracks
  • D. Verify alloy

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: MFL scanners cover large areas of tank floor rapidly during internal inspection, detecting product-side and underside metal loss. Suspect areas are then confirmed with UT prove-up. API 653 references quantitative thresholds (e.g., 20% wall loss).

Question 10: Per API 653, hydrostatic test pressure for a tank after reconstruction is:

  • A. Full liquid head to maximum design liquid level
  • B. 1.5 × design
  • C. No test
  • D. Pneumatic only

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: ASTs are tested by filling with water to the maximum operating liquid level (or the design liquid level for new tanks). API 650 paragraph 7.3.6 provides hydrotest procedures. There is no pressure multiplier; full-head water test demonstrates the static-only loading.

Question 11: An authorized API 653 inspector must:

  • A. Hold current API 653 certification with required experience
  • B. Be the owner
  • C. Hold a PE license
  • D. Be a welder

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: API 653 Section 4 requires current certification under the API ICP program with experience as listed (e.g., BS + 1 yr, AS + 2 yr, HS + 3 yr in NDT/inspection of fixed equipment).

Question 12: An overlay weld repair on a tank bottom is permitted when:

  • A. Per API 653 Section 7 with qualified WPS, NDT, and within thickness/area limits
  • B. Never
  • C. Always
  • D. Only by replacement

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Bottom plate repairs include patch plates (lap-welded or butt-welded), overlay (build-up), or full plate replacement. API 653 Section 9 specifies size limits, weld details, and NDT (typically vacuum box testing on bottom welds).

Question 13: A vacuum box test on a tank bottom weld is performed at:

  • A. 0.21 to 0.55 bar (3 to 8 psi) below atmospheric, with soap solution applied to weld
  • B. 1.5 bar above atmospheric
  • C. No vacuum
  • D. 10 bar

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: API 650 Section 7.3.4 specifies the vacuum box method: apply soap solution, place box over weld, draw partial vacuum (typically 3 to 8 psi). Bubble formation indicates a through-weld leak. Standard for tank bottom welds.

Question 14: Per API 653, a temporary repair is:

  • A. Limited in scope and time, to be replaced with a permanent repair within a defined period
  • B. Permanent
  • C. Not allowed
  • D. Always required

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Temporary repairs (e.g., clamps, doublers) are allowed under API 653 with engineering review and a documented timeline for permanent repair, typically by the next turnaround.

Question 15: Per API RP 651, cathodic protection of tank bottoms uses:

  • A. Galvanic (sacrificial) anodes or impressed current
  • B. Paint only
  • C. Concrete
  • D. No protection

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Underside CP uses either sacrificial anodes (typically Mg or Zn) for small tanks or impressed current systems for larger tanks. Effectiveness measured at −850 mV (Cu/CuSO4 reference) per NACE SP0169 and API RP 651.

Question 16: Per API 653, the minimum interval for ultrasonic thickness measurement of the shell is:

  • A. Calculated from corrosion rate; not to exceed 15 years for tanks without RBI
  • B. Annually
  • C. Once at construction
  • D. 30 years

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: API 653 Section 6.3.3 sets external UT thickness intervals based on corrosion rates: 5 years (uncoated above-grade), 10 years (known low corrosion), 15 years (lined or CP-protected internally), with RBI extensions. External UT can be done while tank is in service.

Question 17: An edge settlement (between bottom and shell) is critical because:

  • A. Bending stresses can cause shell-to-bottom weld cracks
  • B. Only cosmetic
  • C. Improves drainage
  • D. No concern

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Edge settlement (sometimes called dish-out) creates bending of the bottom plates near the shell, generating high secondary stresses at the chime weld. API 653 Annex B provides evaluation criteria based on length and depth.

Question 18: A roof rafter inspection during internal entry must check:

  • A. Section thickness loss, rafter clip attachment, top angle, deck plate corrosion
  • B. Only the column
  • C. Only welds
  • D. Not required

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Fixed cone/dome roof internals: rafters, columns (lateral movement and base plates), top angle, deck plates (corrosion from acidic vapor space), and overflow/vent screens. RP 575 details fixed roof inspection.

Question 19: Per API 653, an API 650 nameplate must be attached to:

  • A. The tank, in a permanent and accessible location
  • B. The piping
  • C. The roof
  • D. Never required

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Per API 650 Section 10, the nameplate identifies manufacturer, year built, design code edition, capacity, maximum operating liquid level, design metal temperature, specific gravity, and the API monogram. Original nameplates must be preserved on reconstruction.

Question 20: A tank that has been out of service for an extended period requires:

  • A. Verification of inspection records, condition assessment, and potential re-inspection before returning to service
  • B. No action
  • C. Always full reconstruction
  • D. Pneumatic test only

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Idle tanks may suffer from internal humidity corrosion, settlement, foundation issues, biological growth. API 653 requires a re-commissioning condition assessment per Section 6 prior to return to service.

Question 21: Per API 653, a release prevention barrier (RPB) is:

  • A. A secondary containment beneath the tank bottom to detect leaks
  • B. A dike
  • C. A vent
  • D. A roof

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: RPB systems (e.g., HDPE liner, concrete pad with leak detection grooves) detect underside leaks and prevent soil/groundwater contamination. EPA SPCC and many state regulations require RPB for new and reconstructed tanks.

Question 22: A linear out-of-roundness on a tank shell can indicate:

  • A. Foundation settlement or wind damage
  • B. Improved capacity
  • C. No concern
  • D. Painted surface

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Tank shell roundness is measured externally with optical or laser methods. Out-of-roundness beyond API 653 limits indicates uneven foundation settlement, wind buckling, vacuum collapse, or installation defects requiring engineering review.

Question 23: Per API 571, atmospheric corrosion of an AST shell is accelerated by:

  • A. Industrial atmosphere, coastal salt, wet/dry cycles, broken paint
  • B. Dry desert
  • C. Vacuum
  • D. Inert gas

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: External atmospheric corrosion accelerates in industrial atmospheres (SO2, NOx), coastal (chlorides), wet/dry cycles, and where paint has failed. Recoating intervals depend on environment severity. API RP 652 covers lining; API 575 covers coating inspection.

Question 24: A tank nozzle stiffening per API 650 is required when:

  • A. The nozzle opening reduces shell pressure-bearing capacity below limits
  • B. Always
  • C. Never
  • D. Owner choice

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Nozzle reinforcement is calculated per API 650 Section 5.7.5 using area replacement rules. Reinforcement plates compensate for removed shell material. Low-type and regular-type nozzle details have prescribed reinforcement.

Question 25: Per API 653 Section 12, hydrostatic testing after major repair is required when:

  • A. The repair affects pressure-containing welds beyond limits specified in Section 12
  • B. Always
  • C. Never
  • D. Owner choice

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: API 653 Section 12 specifies when hydrotest is mandatory after repair/alteration. Generally, replacement of significant shell plate areas, raising tank height, or modifying nozzles in critical zones requires hydrotest. Vacuum box testing is acceptable for bottom-only repairs.

Question 26: A tank double bottom installation is:

  • A. A repair where a new bottom is placed above the existing leaking bottom with annulus monitoring
  • B. New tank
  • C. Not allowed
  • D. Same as RPB

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Double bottom retrofit places a new bottom above the existing bottom with a small annular space (often filled with sand or instrumented for leak detection). This reduces downtime vs full bottom replacement. Engineering review for height/structural impact required.

Question 27: Per API 653, NDT methods commonly used on tanks include:

  • A. VT, UT thickness, MFL floor scan, PT/MT on welds, vacuum box, RT on shell welds
  • B. Only VT
  • C. Only hardness
  • D. Eddy current only

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Tank inspection NDT: VT (mandatory), UT thickness on shell/roof, MFL on floor, PT/MT on critical welds, vacuum box on bottom and annular welds, RT on shell butt welds. PEC for through-coating screening. Settlement survey by total station/laser.

Question 28: Per API 653, a tank weld defect repair requires:

  • A. Excavation to sound metal, NDT to confirm, qualified WPS, post-repair NDT per acceptance criteria
  • B. Cover with paint
  • C. Replacement of full plate
  • D. No repair

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Standard weld repair sequence per ASME IX and API 650/653: excavate defect (grinding or arc gouging), NDT to confirm full removal (typically MT or PT), weld per qualified WPS, post-repair NDT (VT plus MT/PT/RT/UT as specified).

Question 29: Per API 653, the minimum thickness for tank annular ring plate is:

  • A. Calculated based on shell stress, with minimum values per Section 4.5
  • B. 1 mm always
  • C. 50 mm
  • D. No minimum

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Annular plates (the ring of thicker bottom plates beneath the shell) carry high stress from shell. API 653 Section 4.5 sets minimum thickness based on shell stress (S ≤ 23,200 psi gives 6 mm minimum; higher stress requires thicker annular). Stress-relieved welds may be required.

Question 30: A tank inspection report per API 653 must include:

  • A. Findings, calculations, NDT records, photos, repair recommendations, signed by authorized inspector
  • B. Verbal summary only
  • C. Photos only
  • D. Welder names only

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: API 653 Section 13 requires comprehensive inspection records: tank ID and history, measured thicknesses, settlement data, NDT records, deficiencies and recommendations, calculations, photos, and the certified inspector’s signature.

Study Tips for API 653

  • Master settlement analysis: API 653 Annex B is heavily tested. Practice uniform, planar tilt, edge, and out-of-plane settlement evaluation by hand.
  • Tank components vocabulary: Annular ring, sketch plate, chime, knuckle, top angle, wind girder, rafter clip. Misidentifying components is a common exam pitfall.
  • Calculations: Shell thickness by 1-foot method, bottom remaining life, MAOL (maximum allowable operating liquid level), nozzle reinforcement.
  • Damage mechanisms: Underside soil corrosion, MIC, atmospheric, settlement-induced cracking. API 571 sections relevant to tanks.
  • Tab your books: API 653 Sections 4 to 13, API 650 Sections 5 (design) and 7 (fabrication), RP 575, RP 651, RP 652, RP 577.

Recommended Study Materials

  • API 653 Tank Inspection, Repair, Alteration, and Reconstruction
  • API 650 Welded Tanks for Oil Storage
  • API RP 575 Inspection Practices for AST
  • API RP 651 Cathodic Protection of AST
  • API RP 652 Linings for AST Bottoms
  • API RP 577 Welding Inspection and Metallurgy
  • API 571 Damage Mechanisms
  • ASME BPVC V and IX
  • Atlantis NDT API 653 exam preparation course

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What experience is required for API 653?

A: BS + 1 year, AS + 2 years, HS + 3 years of NDT/inspection-related experience on fixed equipment. Verify current API ICP requirements.

Q: What is the difference between API 510, 570, and 653?

A: 510 = pressure vessels, 570 = piping, 653 = aboveground storage tanks. Stacking all three is common for refinery and terminal inspectors.

Q: Is API 653 valid for all tank types?

A: API 653 applies to API 650 / API 12 series welded storage tanks. Riveted tanks and bolted tanks have specific provisions; underground tanks are not in scope (governed by other codes).

Q: How often must a tank be inspected internally?

A: First internal inspection within 10 years if no corrosion data; thereafter based on bottom remaining life; up to 30 years with RBI per API 653 Section 6.4.2.2.

Q: What is a tank API monogram?

A: An API licensee monogram (API 650, 12F, 12D, etc.) certifies the tank was built to the applicable API standard by a licensed shop. Reconstruction work may also be monogrammed.

Q: Does Atlantis NDT offer API 653 review courses?

A: No. Atlantis NDT does not run API 653 exam-preparation courses. Our API 653 tank inspection support is ASNT Level III technical work on tank programmes, not exam coaching.

Q: How does floating roof inspection differ from cone roof?

A: Floating roofs add seals, pontoons, drain hoses, anti-rotation, ladder/stairway, and roof drainage. Cone/dome roofs add rafters, columns, and vent design. Both inspected under API 653 Section 6 and RP 575.

Q: What is the API 653 exam pass rate?

A: Industry first-attempt 50 to 60%; structured prep typically lifts this to 80%+.

Q: Is settlement always rejectable?

A: No — uniform settlement is usually benign. Differential settlement (tilt, edge, out-of-plane) must be evaluated per API 653 Annex B against allowable limits. Engineering review for borderline cases.

Q: How does API 653 relate to ASME B31.3 or API 510/570?

A: API 653 is for storage tanks. ASME B31.3 covers process piping. API 510 covers pressure vessels (over 15 psig). API 570 covers in-service piping. A terminal/refinery inspector typically holds all four.

About Atlantis NDT

Atlantis NDT is a global NDT technology and services company headquartered in Houston, Texas with operations across India and the Middle East. We deliver accredited NDT training, technical consulting, certification preparation, and digital inspection software trusted by oil & gas, fabrication, EPC, and power generation clients. Our team of ASNT Level III instructors has trained thousands of inspectors worldwide.

Whether you are preparing for ASNT certification, API 510, API 570, or API 653, our exam preparation programs combine classroom theory, hands-on practical training, and proctored mock exams that mirror the real test environment.

Call us at +1 (281) 840-8969 or email sales@atlantisndt.com to enroll in the next training cohort. Same-day quotes for corporate group training in Houston, Dubai, Riyadh, Hyderabad, and on-site at your facility.

title: ASNT Level 3 Basic Exam Prep 2026: Format, 25 Practice MCQs, Tips
snippet: Complete 2026 guide to the ASNT Level III Basic exam: format, scope, 25 practice MCQs across all five subject areas, study plan, recommended materials, FAQ.
content:
The ASNT NDT Level III Basic Examination is the foundational exam that every Level III candidate must pass before sitting the method-specific exams. This 2026 guide explains the exam format, scope, and gives 25 practice questions across all five subject areas. References to ASNT CP-189, SNT-TC-1A, ASNT NDT Handbook, applicable ASTM/ISO standards, and the ASNT Body of Knowledge.

ASNT Level III Basic Exam Format Overview

The Basic Exam is a closed-book 135-question, 3-hour computer-based test at a Prometric center. The five subject areas (each ~27 questions) are:

  • Personnel qualification & certification documents: SNT-TC-1A, CP-189, ANSI/ASNT CP-105, ISO 9712
  • NDT methods other than the applicant’s primary methods: a working knowledge of all common NDT methods (UT, RT, MT, PT, VT, ET, LT)
  • Materials, fabrication, and product technology: Metallurgy basics, welding, casting, forging, machining, heat treatment
  • NDT applications and capabilities: What method to use for what defect/material
  • Pass mark: 70% on the combined exam

Once Basic is passed (valid for 5 years), candidates can sit the method exams: UT, RT, MT, PT, VT, ET, LT, and emerging methods (PAUT, AE, IR/T, NR).

ASNT Level III Basic Practice Questions

Question 1: SNT-TC-1A is published by:

  • A. ASNT
  • B. ASTM
  • C. ISO
  • D. API

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: The American Society for Nondestructive Testing publishes SNT-TC-1A (Recommended Practice for Personnel Qualification and Certification in NDT) as a Recommended Practice, not a standard. Employers use it to develop their Written Practice.

Question 2: ASNT CP-189 differs from SNT-TC-1A in that:

  • A. CP-189 is a standard (mandatory when invoked); SNT-TC-1A is a recommended practice
  • B. They are identical
  • C. CP-189 is older
  • D. SNT-TC-1A covers Level III only

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: CP-189 ANSI/ASNT Standard for Qualification and Certification of NDT Personnel is a mandatory standard when contractually invoked. SNT-TC-1A is recommended practice; the employer adapts it via a Written Practice.

Question 3: Per SNT-TC-1A, a Level III may:

  • A. Develop, qualify, and approve procedures; train and certify Level I, II, III personnel; interpret codes
  • B. Only perform inspections
  • C. Only train Level I
  • D. Only sign reports

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: The Level III responsibilities per SNT-TC-1A para 5.3 are broad: develop procedures, approve them, qualify and certify Level I/II/III, interpret codes and specifications, perform NDT, designate NDT methods and techniques.

Question 4: Per SNT-TC-1A, the maximum interval between vision examinations is:

  • A. 12 months
  • B. 5 years
  • C. 10 years
  • D. Once at certification

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: SNT-TC-1A para 8.2 requires annual near vision (Jaeger J1 or equivalent at 12 in / 30 cm) and triennial color vision exam. CP-189 has similar requirements.

Question 5: Which NDT method is best suited for detecting subsurface laminations in plate steel?

  • A. Ultrasonic testing (UT)
  • B. Liquid penetrant (PT)
  • C. Magnetic particle (MT)
  • D. Visual

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Subsurface laminations parallel to the rolled plate surface are detected by straight beam UT (loss of backwall echo and intermediate echoes). MT and PT can only detect surface-breaking flaws.

Question 6: Eddy current testing (ET) is most useful for:

  • A. Conductive material surface and near-surface flaws, coating thickness, sorting alloys
  • B. Subsurface in non-conductive material
  • C. Concrete
  • D. Wood

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: ET works on electrically conductive materials. It detects surface and near-surface cracks (limited by skin depth, typically 1 to 5 mm), measures conductivity (alloy sorting), and measures non-conductive coating thickness over conductive substrate.

Question 7: Carbon steel has a typical Curie point of:

  • A. 770°C
  • B. 100°C
  • C. 1500°C
  • D. 50°C

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Above the Curie temperature (~770°C for iron), the material becomes paramagnetic. Below it is ferromagnetic. MT cannot be performed above the Curie point.

Question 8: Which welding process is most prone to hydrogen-induced cracking (HIC) if not properly controlled?

  • A. SMAW (stick) with damp electrodes
  • B. TIG (GTAW)
  • C. Brazing
  • D. Friction stir welding

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: SMAW with low-hydrogen electrodes that have absorbed moisture (or non-low-hydrogen electrodes) introduces hydrogen into the weld. HIC develops in the HAZ of hardenable steels. Electrode storage and baking is critical.

Question 9: A cast steel part may have which characteristic defect?

  • A. Shrinkage cavities, gas porosity, hot tears, cold shuts, inclusions
  • B. Only fatigue
  • C. Only stress corrosion
  • D. No defects possible

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Casting defects (per ASTM E446, E186, E280) include shrinkage (centerline, dendritic), porosity (gas), hot tears (high-temperature cracking), cold shuts (failure of two metal streams to fuse), and inclusions. RT is the primary NDT for castings.

Question 10: A forged steel part typically has:

  • A. Refined grain structure with flow lines, fewer defects than castings
  • B. Always cracked
  • C. Identical to castings
  • D. No grain structure

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Forging plastically deforms the material, refining grain structure and aligning flow lines along the principal stress direction. Forged parts have higher fatigue and toughness than castings of the same alloy. Typical defects: laps, seams, internal bursts.

Question 11: ASTM E94 is a standard guide for:

  • A. Radiographic examination
  • B. Ultrasonic
  • C. Magnetic particle
  • D. Penetrant

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: ASTM E94 (now superseded by parts of E1742, E1815, E2033, E2698) is the standard guide for radiographic examination. ASNT Level III candidates must know which ASTM standard governs each method.

Question 12: ISO 9712 is the international standard for:

  • A. NDT personnel qualification and certification
  • B. Welding consumables
  • C. Pressure vessels
  • D. Tank inspection

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: ISO 9712 is the international NDT personnel qualification and certification standard, providing third-party certification (PCN, COFREND, etc.). It differs from SNT-TC-1A (employer-based US scheme).

Question 13: Charpy V-notch impact testing measures:

  • A. Notch toughness and ductile-to-brittle transition
  • B. Hardness only
  • C. Tensile strength only
  • D. Density

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Charpy testing strikes a notched specimen with a swinging pendulum at controlled temperatures, measuring energy absorbed. Used to determine ductile-to-brittle transition temperature and minimum design metal temperature.

Question 14: Quenching and tempering (Q&T) of steel produces:

  • A. High hardness/strength tempered to acceptable toughness
  • B. Maximum ductility only
  • C. Annealed structure
  • D. No change

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Quenching from austenitizing temperature forms hard martensite. Tempering at intermediate temperatures (typically 400 to 700°C) reduces brittleness while retaining significant strength. Common for pressure equipment, fasteners, gears.

Question 15: Acoustic emission (AE) testing detects:

  • A. Energy released during active material processes (crack growth, leak, deformation)
  • B. Static thickness
  • C. Surface roughness
  • D. Color

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: AE is a passive method: sensors detect transient elastic waves from active discontinuities (growing cracks, leaking joints, plastic deformation, corrosion product cracking). Used for tank floor leak testing, pressure vessel testing, bridge monitoring.

Question 16: Per SNT-TC-1A, training requirements for direct entry Level II:

  • A. Sum of Level I + Level II training and experience required
  • B. Only Level II training
  • C. No requirements
  • D. Level III approval only

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: SNT-TC-1A para 6.4 allows direct entry to Level II if the candidate satisfies the cumulative training and experience for Level I + Level II. The Written Practice must specifically permit this.

Question 17: Radiation safety units of equivalent dose are:

  • A. Sievert (Sv) and rem (1 Sv = 100 rem)
  • B. Gray and rad
  • C. Becquerel
  • D. Roentgen

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Equivalent dose accounts for radiation type and biological effect. SI unit Sievert, traditional rem. Absorbed dose units: Gray (SI), rad (traditional). Activity units: Becquerel (SI), Curie (traditional). Exposure: Coulomb/kg or Roentgen.

Question 18: A martensitic stainless steel (e.g., 410, 420) is:

  • A. Ferromagnetic and hardenable by heat treatment
  • B. Non-magnetic
  • C. Always soft
  • D. Cannot be welded

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Martensitic stainless (400 series) is ferromagnetic and can be hardened by Q&T. MT and PT both usable. Austenitic (300 series) is non-magnetic, not hardenable by heat treatment, but work-hardenable.

Question 19: Per SNT-TC-1A, a Level II inspector may:

  • A. Set up and calibrate equipment, perform inspections, interpret results, train Level I
  • B. Approve procedures
  • C. Certify Level III
  • D. Develop new methods

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Per para 5.2, Level II personnel are qualified to set up and calibrate equipment, perform tests per established procedures, interpret and evaluate, organize and report results, and provide on-the-job training to Level I personnel.

Question 20: The phenomenon of resonance in UT is used in:

  • A. Thin-wall thickness measurement
  • B. Subsurface defect detection
  • C. Surface roughness
  • D. Hardness

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Resonance occurs when a continuous wave is reflected back in phase between the front and back surfaces. Half-wavelength multiples of thickness produce resonance. Used historically for thin-wall thickness; now mostly replaced by pulse-echo digital gauges.

Question 21: A typical austenitic stainless steel grade is:

  • A. 304 or 316
  • B. 410
  • C. 4140
  • D. 6061

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: 304 (18Cr-8Ni) and 316 (18Cr-10Ni-2Mo) are common austenitic stainless steels. 410/420 are martensitic. 4140 is low-alloy carbon steel. 6061 is aluminum alloy.

Question 22: Welding heat-affected zone (HAZ) typically has:

  • A. Altered microstructure and properties due to thermal cycle
  • B. Same as base metal
  • C. Same as weld metal
  • D. No properties

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: The HAZ experiences temperatures from ambient (at the unaffected base metal boundary) up to the melting point (at the fusion line), creating microstructural gradients: grain growth, recrystallization, partial transformation. Often the most defect-prone region.

Question 23: Per CP-189, training records must be retained for:

  • A. Period specified by the employer’s quality system, typically the employee’s career plus several years
  • B. Until the employee leaves
  • C. No retention required
  • D. 1 year

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Personnel qualification records (training, experience, exams, vision, hands-on demonstration) must be retained per the employer’s documented quality system. Many industries (aerospace, nuclear) specify decades of retention.

Question 24: ISO 9712 certification is administered by:

  • A. Independent certification bodies (e.g., BINDT/PCN, COFREND, DGZfP)
  • B. The employer
  • C. The trainee
  • D. ASTM

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: ISO 9712 is a third-party certification model: the certification body is independent of both the employer and the candidate. PCN, COFREND, DGZfP, and ACCP are well-known schemes. Compare with our ASNT vs PCN article.

Question 25: A Level III may be qualified by:

  • A. ASNT third-party Level III exam (ACCP/Level III) or employer-administered exam under SNT-TC-1A
  • B. Self-declaration
  • C. Years of experience alone
  • D. Single training course

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Most US Level IIIs hold the ASNT Level III certificate (Basic + Method exam, third-party administered). Under SNT-TC-1A, employers may also certify Level III, but most customers and codes (ASME, API) require ASNT Level III certificate.

Study Tips for the ASNT Level III Basic Exam

  • Cover all five subject areas evenly: Don’t over-focus on your primary method — you must score well across all five areas.
  • SNT-TC-1A and CP-189 paragraph by paragraph: Many candidates miss easy points on personnel qualification basics. Memorize paragraph numbers.
  • Learn cross-method knowledge: Even if you are a UT Level II, you must answer RT, MT, PT, ET, VT, LT questions confidently.
  • Materials science: Basic metallurgy, welding, casting, forging, heat treatment. The ASNT Level III Study Guide covers this well.
  • NDT applications: Know what method suits what defect/material. Practice scenario questions.

Recommended Study Materials

  • ASNT Level III Study Guide: Basic Examination
  • ASNT Recommended Practice SNT-TC-1A
  • ANSI/ASNT CP-189 Standard
  • ASNT NDT Handbook Volume 10 (Overview)
  • ISO 9712:2021 standard
  • ASTM Standards (E94, E709, E165, E1444, etc.)
  • Atlantis NDT Level III Basic exam preparation course

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: How many questions on the ASNT Level III Basic exam?

A: 135 multiple-choice questions, 3 hours, closed-book, computer-based at Prometric.

Q: What is the pass mark for the Basic exam?

A: 70% overall. Some employers require higher composite scores combining Basic and Method exams.

Q: How long is the Basic exam valid?

A: 5 years. The candidate must pass at least one Method exam within this period to obtain Level III status. The Basic remains valid as long as at least one Method certificate is active.

Q: Can I take the Method exam without passing the Basic first?

A: No. Basic must be passed before the corresponding Method exam.

Q: How many ASNT Level III methods can I hold?

A: Unlimited — many Level IIIs hold UT, RT, MT, PT, VT, and ET. Each method requires its own Method exam after the Basic.

Q: Is ASNT Level III the same as PCN Level 3?

A: They are equivalent in industry recognition but follow different schemes. ASNT is employer-based or ACCP third-party (US); PCN is third-party (UK/global). See our ASNT vs PCN comparison.

Q: Does Atlantis NDT prepare candidates for the ASNT Level III Basic?

A: Yes — our 5-day Level III Basic prep course includes 500+ practice questions across all five subject areas, code/standard reference workshop, and a mock exam. Cohorts in Houston, Dubai, and on-site. Call +1 (281) 840-8969 to enroll.

Q: What is the typical Level III pass rate?

A: First-attempt pass rate for the Basic averages 50 to 65%. Atlantis prep students average 80%+.

Q: How much does a Level III earn?

A: US Level III $110,000 to $180,000+/year base; Middle East a modest cost to a modest cost/month tax-free. Multiple-method Level IIIs (UT, RT, MT, PT) command top of range. See L2 vs L3 article.

Q: Are there continuing education requirements for Level III?

A: ASNT does not mandate CEUs for renewal, but recertification at year 5 (and 10) requires re-examination unless the candidate accumulates points under the Recertification Through Points option.

About Atlantis NDT

We deliver accredited NDT training, technical consulting, certification preparation, and digital inspection software trusted by oil & gas, fabrication, EPC, and power generation clients. Our team of ASNT Level III instructors has trained thousands of inspectors worldwide.

title: CSWIP 3.1 Exam Prep 2026: Format, 25 Practice MCQs, Study Guide
snippet: Complete 2026 CSWIP 3.1 welding inspector prep: exam format, 25 practice MCQs, defect identification, code references (AWS D1.1, ASME IX, EN ISO 5817), FAQ.
content:
The CSWIP 3.1 Welding Inspector certification is one of the most widely recognized welding inspector qualifications worldwide. Administered by TWI Certification Ltd (UK), it covers welding inspection of structural and pressure equipment in line with international codes. This 2026 guide explains the exam, gives 25 practice questions, and provides study and reference material guidance.

CSWIP 3.1 Exam Format Overview

CSWIP 3.1 is a 5-day course concluding with multiple examinations:

  • General Theory (Paper 1): 50 multiple-choice questions, 1 hour, 70% pass mark. Covers welding processes, terminology, defects, materials, NDT awareness.
  • Specific Theory (Paper 2): 60 multiple-choice questions, 1 hour 15 minutes, 70%. Covers a chosen code/standard (e.g., AWS D1.1, BS EN ISO 5817, ASME IX) applied to inspection.
  • Practical Plates and Pipes: Two practical examinations: visual inspection of a butt-welded plate and butt-welded pipe, report findings. 70% on each.
  • Macro Examination: Identify weld features and defects from polished and etched macro sections. 70%.
  • Overall: All sections must be passed to gain CSWIP 3.1.

Certification valid for 5 years; renewal at 5 years requires renewal exam (re-test of theory) and continued practice records. Full re-exam at 10 years.

CSWIP 3.1 Practice Questions

Question 1: SMAW is the abbreviation for:

  • A. Shielded Metal Arc Welding (stick welding, MMA)
  • B. Submerged Metal Arc Welding
  • C. Single Metal Arc Welding
  • D. Stainless Metal Arc Welding

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: SMAW (AWS designation) = Shielded Metal Arc Welding, also known as Manual Metal Arc (MMA) in UK/European usage. Uses a consumable flux-coated electrode. Versatile, simple, widely used.

Question 2: GTAW is also known as:

  • A. TIG (Tungsten Inert Gas) welding
  • B. MIG welding
  • C. Stick welding
  • D. Brazing

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: GTAW = Gas Tungsten Arc Welding = TIG. Uses a non-consumable tungsten electrode and inert shielding gas (argon, helium). Filler is added separately. Produces high-quality welds in stainless, aluminum, and root passes on pipe.

Question 3: Lack of fusion at the side wall is caused by:

  • A. Insufficient heat, poor electrode angle, contamination
  • B. Too much penetration
  • C. Cold weather only
  • D. Excessive cleaning

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Lack of side-wall fusion (LOF) occurs when the molten pool does not melt the parent metal at the joint side. Caused by insufficient heat input, wrong electrode angle, fast travel speed, slag/contamination on side wall. Critical defect, usually rejected.

Question 4: A weld defect that appears as a thin line of slag entrapment between weld passes is:

  • A. Inter-run slag (slag inclusion)
  • B. Porosity
  • C. Crack
  • D. Undercut

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Slag inclusions between weld runs (inter-run slag) occur when slag is not properly cleaned between passes in SMAW, FCAW, or SAW. Appears on RT as irregular dark indications usually following the bead.

Question 5: Undercut is:

  • A. A groove melted into the parent material adjacent to a weld toe
  • B. Excess weld metal
  • C. Porosity
  • D. Internal flaw

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Undercut is a surface flaw: a groove melted into the parent metal adjacent to the weld toe, not filled by weld metal. Common in high-current GMAW and SMAW. Acceptance limits in BS EN ISO 5817 are based on weld class.

Question 6: BS EN ISO 5817 quality level B is:

  • A. Stringent (most strict)
  • B. Moderate
  • C. Loose
  • D. No requirements

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: BS EN ISO 5817 defines three quality levels: B (stringent), C (intermediate), D (moderate). Higher levels have tighter acceptance criteria on every defect type. Most pressure equipment specifies B or C.

Question 7: A weld procedure specification (WPS) per ASME IX must include:

  • A. Essential and non-essential variables for the process
  • B. Only the welder’s name
  • C. Material thickness only
  • D. Visual inspector only

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: ASME IX QW-200 requires the WPS to list essential, supplementary essential, and non-essential variables (process, base metal, filler metal, position, preheat, PWHT, gas, electrical, technique). Changes to essential variables require requalification (new PQR).

Question 8: A PQR (Procedure Qualification Record) is:

  • A. Documentation of the actual welding parameters and mechanical tests used to qualify a WPS
  • B. A pre-job checklist
  • C. Material spec
  • D. Welder ID card

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: The PQR records the actual values used (current, voltage, travel speed, preheat, etc.) during qualification welding and the test results (tensile, bend, impact, hardness). The WPS is derived from the PQR.

Question 9: A welder performance qualification (WPQ) per ASME IX is:

  • A. The record that the welder produced a sound test coupon meeting acceptance criteria
  • B. A union card
  • C. The WPS
  • D. A heat treatment record

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: WPQ (QW-300) demonstrates the welder’s skill. Welder welds a coupon per the WPS; the coupon is tested (RT or bend tests). Acceptance qualifies the welder for a range of positions, materials, and thicknesses per the essential variables.

Question 10: A welder continuity period per ASME IX is:

  • A. Maximum 6 months between welds in the qualified process to maintain certification
  • B. No limit
  • C. 12 months
  • D. Forever

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Per QW-322, a welder must weld using the qualified process at least every 6 months to maintain qualification. If gap exceeds 6 months, requalification is required (or limited recertification per QW-322.2).

Question 11: A typical preheat temperature for carbon steel above 25 mm thick is:

  • A. 100 to 150°C, with higher for higher carbon equivalent
  • B. No preheat needed
  • C. Above 500°C
  • D. Cool below ambient

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Preheat reduces cooling rate to prevent hard HAZ and hydrogen cracking. AWS D1.1, ASME B31.3, ISO/TR 17671 provide preheat tables based on material, thickness, carbon equivalent, and heat input.

Question 12: A solidification crack (hot crack) typically:

  • A. Forms in the weld metal during solidification, usually centerline
  • B. Forms cold in the HAZ
  • C. Forms after PWHT
  • D. Does not occur

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Hot cracks form at high temperature during solidification, typically along grain boundaries at the weld centerline. Driven by tensile stress and segregation of impurities (sulfur, phosphorus). Mitigated by reducing restraint, decreasing heat input, controlling impurities.

Question 13: A cold crack (hydrogen crack) in HAZ typically appears:

  • A. Hours or days after welding, in hard microstructure with hydrogen and tensile stress
  • B. During welding only
  • C. Never
  • D. Always at root

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Hydrogen-assisted cold cracking requires hydrogen, hard microstructure (martensite), and tensile stress. Develops typically 48 hours after welding. Prevention: low-hydrogen consumables, preheat, hydrogen bake-out, controlled cooling, soft microstructure (PWHT).

Question 14: A weld root concavity is:

  • A. A shallow groove at the weld root, less than parent metal level
  • B. Excess penetration
  • C. Slag
  • D. Porosity

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Root concavity is a depression at the root surface caused by excessive penetration heat or insufficient filler. Acceptance depends on code; usually limited to 1 to 2 mm depending on wall thickness.

Question 15: A weld toe is:

  • A. The junction between weld face and parent metal
  • B. The root
  • C. The weld cap
  • D. The heat source

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: The weld toe is where the weld surface meets the base metal. Stress concentrates here, making toes preferential sites for fatigue cracks. Toe grinding/peening is a common fatigue improvement technique.

Question 16: Per AWS D1.1, visual inspection of welds is performed:

  • A. Always — mandatory for all welds
  • B. Optional
  • C. Only on completed pressure vessels
  • D. Never

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Visual inspection is the most universal NDT method. AWS D1.1, ASME IX, and BS EN ISO 17637 all mandate visual inspection on all welds. CSWIP 3.1 is fundamentally a visual inspector qualification.

Question 17: A weld with high crown reinforcement:

  • A. Creates stress concentration and is typically limited in height
  • B. Improves strength
  • C. Is required
  • D. Has no effect

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Excess weld metal (overfill) creates a notch at the weld toe, raising stress concentration. Codes typically limit cap height to 3 mm for thin sections and up to 5 mm for thicker plates. Grinding flush is common for fatigue-critical applications.

Question 18: PWHT (post-weld heat treatment) of carbon steel typically holds at:

  • A. 580 to 620°C for stress relief
  • B. Above melting
  • C. Below freezing
  • D. Room temperature

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: PWHT for carbon steel holds at 580 to 620°C for typically 1 hour per inch of thickness. Reduces residual stress, tempers HAZ, helps hydrogen diffusion. Heating/cooling rate controlled to limit thermal stress.

Question 19: A fillet weld leg length is measured:

  • A. From the toe to the root along each fusion face
  • B. Diagonal of the weld
  • C. Width only
  • D. Not measured

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Fillet weld leg = distance from the joint root to the toe along each fusion face. Throat = shortest distance from the root to the weld face. Most acceptance criteria specify minimum leg length.

Question 20: Gas tungsten arc welding (GTAW/TIG) shielding gas is typically:

  • A. Argon, or argon-helium mixtures
  • B. CO2
  • C. Air
  • D. Nitrogen for steel

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: TIG uses inert gas to protect the tungsten and weld pool. Argon is the most common (cleaner arc, easier control); helium adds heat (deeper penetration). CO2 is reactive and not used for TIG. Nitrogen used for duplex stainless backing in limited applications.

Question 21: A welder qualified on plate (PA position) by ASME IX is also qualified for:

  • A. Plate flat (PA) position only, per essential variable position
  • B. All positions
  • C. Pipe in all positions
  • D. No position

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Position is an essential variable for welder qualification. Plate PA qualifies only flat. To qualify for vertical/overhead, the welder must test in those positions. Pipe 6G qualifies all positions.

Question 22: A typical filler metal classification AWS A5.1 E7018 indicates:

  • A. 70 ksi tensile, all positions, low-hydrogen iron-powder iron-powder coating, AC/DCEP
  • B. Aluminum
  • C. Stainless steel
  • D. Cast iron

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: AWS A5.1 SMAW electrode classification: E = electrode, 70 = 70 ksi tensile, 1 = all positions, 8 = iron-powder iron-powder low-hydrogen flux. E7018 is the workhorse low-hydrogen electrode for carbon steel pressure work.

Question 23: A weld macro examination requires:

  • A. Cut section, polish, etch with appropriate reagent, examine at low magnification
  • B. Microscopic only
  • C. Photograph weld surface
  • D. Heat treat the weld

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: CSWIP 3.1 macro exam: cut weld coupon transverse to the weld, polish with progressively finer papers (220, 400, 600 grit), etch with 2% Nital (carbon steel), examine the cross-section for fusion, defects, HAZ size, and pass sequence. Magnification typically 5x to 10x.

Question 24: A weld inspection report should include:

  • A. Job ID, welder, WPS, NDT performed, indications with location and acceptance status, inspector ID and date
  • B. Verbal report only
  • C. Sketch only
  • D. Welder name only

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Standard weld inspection report includes traceability (job, drawing, weld number), welder identification, WPS/PQR reference, NDT performed, all indications with size and location, acceptance per code, repair recommendations, and inspector identification.

Question 25: A CSWIP 3.1 inspector’s primary role is:

  • A. Verify welding is performed per WPS and that the resulting weld meets the acceptance code
  • B. Welding
  • C. Designing welds
  • D. Heat treatment

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: CSWIP 3.1 inspectors check that the WPS is used, parameters are within limits, joint preparation is correct, NDT is performed, and the finished weld meets the visual and NDT acceptance criteria. They do not weld or design.

Study Tips for CSWIP 3.1

  • Memorize defect morphology: Use the TWI defect chart, read BS EN ISO 6520-1 (defect classification). Be able to identify every common weld defect from a photo or macro.
  • Master the code: Choose your code (AWS D1.1, ASME IX, BS EN ISO 5817) and study it cover to cover. The Specific Theory paper is open-book for some codes.
  • Practical practice: Spend 20+ hours visually inspecting real welded plates and pipes before the exam. Practice writing concise, accurate inspection reports.
  • Macro etching: Practice etching and identifying features on sample sections. Most candidates fail the macro paper because they cannot identify all weld passes.
  • Time management: The General Theory is 50 questions in 60 minutes; less than 1.5 minutes per question. Pace yourself.

Recommended Study Materials

  • TWI CSWIP 3.1 Course Notes (provided at training)
  • BS EN ISO 5817 Quality levels for imperfections in welded joints
  • BS EN ISO 6520-1 Classification of geometric imperfections
  • ASME BPVC IX Welding qualification
  • AWS D1.1 Structural Welding Code
  • BS EN ISO 17637 Visual testing of fusion welds
  • Atlantis NDT CSWIP 3.1 prep course (5-day course aligned with TWI syllabus)

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: How is CSWIP 3.1 different from CSWIP 3.0?

A: CSWIP 3.0 is the entry-level Visual Welding Inspector (limited to visual inspection of butt and fillet welds in plate). CSWIP 3.1 expands to pipes and adds the macro examination. CSWIP 3.2 (Senior Welding Inspector) is the next step up.

Q: Is CSWIP 3.1 recognized in the USA?

A: CSWIP 3.1 is widely recognized globally, including in many US oil & gas, pipeline, and offshore contracts. AWS CWI (Certified Welding Inspector) is the closest US equivalent and is sometimes preferred for AWS-driven structural work.

Q: What experience is required to sit CSWIP 3.1?

A: Documented experience in welding inspection, with formal training of at least one week prior. Typical candidates have 1+ year of welding/inspection background.

Q: How long does CSWIP 3.1 certification last?

A: 5 years initial certification, renewable at 5 years with continued practice records and a re-examination. Full reset exam at 10 years.

Q: How does CSWIP 3.1 differ from API 510/570?

A: CSWIP 3.1 is a welding inspection certification, focused on construction-stage QA/QC. API 510/570/653 are in-service inspection certifications. Many inspectors hold both for full life-cycle coverage.

Q: Does Atlantis NDT offer CSWIP 3.1 prep courses?

A: Yes — our 5-day intensive CSWIP 3.1 prep course mirrors the TWI syllabus, includes 300+ practice questions, mock macro exams, and real plates/pipes for practical practice. Cohorts run quarterly in Houston, Dubai, Hyderabad. Call +1 (281) 840-8969.

Q: What is the CSWIP 3.1 pass rate?

A: First-attempt pass rate averages 65 to 75%. The macro paper has the highest failure rate. Atlantis prep students average 90%+.

Q: Can I take CSWIP 3.1 without prior welding experience?

A: It is allowed but very challenging. We recommend at least 1 year of welding QC/QA experience before attempting CSWIP 3.1.

Q: Is CSWIP 3.1 valid for NDT inspection?

A: CSWIP 3.1 covers visual inspection of welds. For NDT methods (UT, RT, MT, PT), separate ASNT or PCN certifications are required. See our ASNT vs PCN article.

Q: How does CSWIP 3.1 compare to AWS CWI?

A: Both are welding inspector certifications. CSWIP is UK-origin, internationally recognized in oil & gas and offshore. AWS CWI is US-origin, dominant in US structural and pipeline. Many inspectors hold both.

title: PCN Level 2 Exam Guide 2026: Format, 25 Practice MCQs, ISO 9712
snippet: 2026 PCN Level 2 NDT exam guide: ISO 9712 alignment, exam structure, 25 practice MCQs, sectors, vision rules, recertification, study tips, and FAQ.
content:
The Personnel Certification in Non-destructive Testing (PCN) scheme, administered by the British Institute of Non-Destructive Testing (BINDT), is one of the most widely recognized third-party NDT certifications globally. PCN is fully aligned with ISO 9712, and a PCN Level 2 certificate is accepted across Europe, the Middle East, Asia, and increasingly North America. This 2026 guide explains the PCN Level 2 exam structure, gives practice questions for the most common methods (UT, RT, MT, PT), and provides recommended study material.

PCN Level 2 Exam Format Overview

PCN Level 2 follows ISO 9712 closely. The certification structure has three components:

  • General Examination: 40 closed-book MCQ on NDT principles for the chosen method. 1 hour 30 minutes. Pass mark 70%.
  • Specific Examination: 30 closed-book MCQ covering codes/standards and product technology relevant to the candidate’s industry sector. 1 hour 30 minutes. Pass mark 70%.
  • Practical Examination: Hands-on demonstration including instrument setup, calibration, inspection of two or three specimens, written report on findings, and writing an NDT instruction. 80% pass mark on practical (separate elements: instruction writing, setup, indication detection, evaluation, reporting).

All three components must be passed in the same window (typically 1 year). Certification valid for 5 years with annual employer verification of practice, renewal exam at 5 years, full recertification at 10 years.

PCN Industry Sectors

PCN organizes certifications by industry sector. Common Level 2 sectors include:

  • Welds: Pressure equipment, structural welds, pipelines
  • Castings: Steel, aluminum castings
  • Forgings: Steel, aluminum forgings
  • Wrought: Plate, rod, bar inspection
  • Aerospace: Combination of welds, castings, composites
  • Railway: Wheel/axle inspection, rail integrity
  • In-service inspection: Pressure equipment, pipelines, tanks

PCN Level 2 Practice Questions

Question 1: PCN is administered by:

  • A. BINDT (British Institute of Non-Destructive Testing)
  • B. ASNT
  • C. TWI
  • D. ISO directly

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: BINDT, headquartered in Northampton UK, administers the PCN scheme. PCN is fully ISO 9712 aligned and accredited by UKAS (UK Accreditation Service).

Question 2: PCN Level 2 certification follows which international standard?

  • A. ISO 9712
  • B. ASNT SNT-TC-1A
  • C. EN 473 (now obsolete)
  • D. ASME Section V

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: ISO 9712 is the international standard for NDT personnel qualification. PCN is one of several ISO 9712-compliant schemes (others include COFREND, DGZfP, ACCP). EN 473 was the former European standard, now harmonized with ISO 9712.

Question 3: How long is PCN Level 2 certification initially valid?

  • A. 5 years
  • B. 10 years
  • C. 1 year
  • D. 3 years

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: ISO 9712 sets the certification cycle at 5 years initial validity, renewal at 5 years (administrative renewal with annual eye exam and continuous practice), and full recertification exam at 10 years.

Question 4: PCN UT Level 2 weld sector requires what minimum experience?

  • A. 480 hours UT experience documented (after Level 1) before sitting Level 2
  • B. No experience required
  • C. 10 years
  • D. 100 hours

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: ISO 9712 Table 2 / PCN appendix sets experience: typically 480 hours UT Level 2 documented after Level 1 certification, plus 80 hours formal training. Direct-entry Level 2 requires combined Level 1 + 2 training and experience.

Question 5: For a PCN UT Level 2 weld inspection at 60°, the skip distance on 25 mm plate is:

  • A. ~86.6 mm full skip (2 × 25 × tan 60°)
  • B. 50 mm
  • C. 25 mm
  • D. 100 mm

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Full skip = 2 × thickness × tan(angle) = 2 × 25 × 1.732 = 86.6 mm. Half skip = 43.3 mm. Skip distances are critical for marking the scanning range for full coverage of the weld volume.

Question 6: A PCN UT Level 2 specific examination weld sector uses what standard for acceptance?

  • A. EN ISO 11666 or EN ISO 23279, depending on contract
  • B. ASNT only
  • C. No standard
  • D. AWS only

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: European weld acceptance standards: EN ISO 11666 (acceptance for amplitude-based UT), EN ISO 23279 (characterization of indications), EN ISO 17640 (general UT of welds). ASME and AWS are also recognized depending on contract.

Question 7: A PCN RT Level 2 candidate must demonstrate competence in:

  • A. Setup, exposure calculation, processing, IQI sensitivity verification, interpretation, reporting
  • B. Only film handling
  • C. Only safety
  • D. Only writing

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: PCN RT Level 2 practical demonstration covers the full workflow: technique selection, IQI placement, exposure setup, film processing or DR/CR acquisition, interpretation, and final report. All must reach 80% to pass.

Question 8: PCN Level 2 in MT requires understanding of:

  • A. Magnetization methods, field strength verification, particle systems, indication interpretation, acceptance criteria
  • B. Only one technique
  • C. Only welds
  • D. Only forgings

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: PCN MT Level 2 covers all magnetization techniques (yoke, prod, coil, central conductor, head shot, multidirectional), particle types (visible/fluorescent, wet/dry), field strength verification, and acceptance to applicable standards (e.g., EN ISO 23278).

Question 9: A PCN PT Level 2 practical exam typically includes:

  • A. Pre-clean, penetrant, dwell, removal, developer, evaluate, report on 2 to 3 specimens
  • B. Only spray penetrant
  • C. Only visual
  • D. No specimens

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: PCN PT Level 2 practical follows the full penetrant sequence on 2 or 3 specimens (typically with planted defects). Candidates must identify and characterize indications, evaluate to the chosen acceptance standard (EN ISO 23277 etc.).

Question 10: PCN Level 2 certificate is recognized in:

  • A. UK, Europe, Middle East, Asia, increasingly worldwide oil & gas
  • B. UK only
  • C. US only
  • D. Nowhere

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: PCN is globally recognized in oil & gas (Shell, BP, ADNOC, Aramco accept PCN), offshore, pipelines, manufacturing, and aerospace. ISO 9712 alignment makes PCN portable across borders.

Question 11: A PCN written NDT instruction is:

  • A. A document a Level 2 prepares from an approved procedure, specifying step-by-step how to perform an inspection on a specific item
  • B. The same as a procedure
  • C. A welding spec
  • D. A safety document

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Per ISO 9712 / PCN, Level 2 personnel are authorized to write NDT instructions from approved procedures. The instruction is item-specific and lists exact parameters, scope, and acceptance. Level 2 cannot write procedures (that is Level 3).

Question 12: PCN vision requirements per ISO 9712 are:

  • A. Near vision Jaeger 1 or equivalent at 30 cm, plus color vision triennial
  • B. Color only
  • C. No requirements
  • D. Distance vision only

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: ISO 9712 / PCN requires near vision capable of reading Jaeger 1 or Times Roman N4.5 letters at 30 cm (one or both eyes, corrected if needed), and color vision sufficient to distinguish colors used in the method (triennial test).

Question 13: PCN recertification at 10 years requires:

  • A. Re-examination (general, specific, and practical)
  • B. Document review only
  • C. No action
  • D. Just experience hours

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: ISO 9712 specifies 10-year recertification by re-examination, similar to the initial qualifying exams. Renewal at 5 years is by document review (continued practice, eye exam, employer endorsement) with no exam.

Question 14: PCN practical examination for UT Level 2 typically includes how many specimens?

  • A. Two or three specimens of the chosen sector (e.g., two weld specimens + one cast)
  • B. One
  • C. Ten
  • D. None

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: ISO 9712 Annex A and PCN procedures specify the minimum 2 specimens for many sectors, with extra for multi-process sectors. Weld sector typically requires plate butt weld and pipe butt weld specimens.

Question 15: PCN Level 2 specific paper open-book or closed?

  • A. Closed-book by default (some sectors may allow access to specific standards)
  • B. Always open-book
  • C. No specific paper
  • D. Verbal only

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: PCN specific exams are closed-book in most sectors (candidates must memorize key acceptance values), although some sectors allow restricted reference material. Always verify with the current PCN syllabus.

Question 16: A PCN Level 2 weld sector candidate must know acceptance to which European standards?

  • A. EN ISO 5817 (visual quality levels), EN ISO 11666 (UT acceptance), EN ISO 10675 (RT), EN ISO 23277 (PT), EN ISO 23278 (MT)
  • B. Only ASME
  • C. AWS only
  • D. No standards

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: The European/ISO acceptance standards form the spec backbone of PCN weld sector exams. Candidates must memorize quality levels (B, C, D) and key acceptance values.

Question 17: A PCN training course must be conducted by:

  • A. A PCN-approved training organization (ATO)
  • B. Any company
  • C. Self-study only
  • D. Online only

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: ISO 9712 requires training by an approved training organization. PCN maintains a register of ATOs that have demonstrated trainer qualifications, syllabus alignment, and facilities. Atlantis NDT is working toward formal ATO status; for now we deliver pre-PCN preparation training in partnership with ATOs.

Question 18: PCN Level 2 UT training duration is typically:

  • A. 80 hours (40 Level 1 + 40 Level 2) total
  • B. 8 hours
  • C. 200 hours
  • D. No formal training

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: ISO 9712 Table 1 specifies 40 hours UT Level 1 + 40 hours UT Level 2 = 80 hours total formal training. Other methods have different durations (e.g., MT 12 + 8, PT 4 + 8, RT 40 + 40).

Question 19: PCN Level 2 in PAUT (Phased Array UT) sector is:

  • A. Separate from standard UT — requires its own training and exam
  • B. Same as standard UT
  • C. No certification exists
  • D. Only Level 3

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: PCN treats PAUT as a separate method requiring its own qualifying exam (general, specific, practical). Candidates typically must hold PCN UT Level 2 in the same sector first. See our PAUT vs TOFD article.

Question 20: PCN compared to ASNT employer-based certification is:

  • A. Third-party (independent of employer), generally more portable internationally
  • B. Same as ASNT
  • C. Inferior
  • D. Only US

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: PCN is third-party certification (BINDT, not the employer, issues the certificate). ASNT employer-based (SNT-TC-1A) is issued by the employer and is tied to that employer. ACCP and ASNT Central Certification are third-party schemes. See ASNT vs PCN article.

Question 21: A PCN candidate’s vision results must be:

  • A. Verified by a qualified medical examiner annually
  • B. Self-declared
  • C. Only at certification
  • D. Not required

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Vision must be verified by an optometrist, occupational physician, or other competent medical examiner annually. Color vision is verified every 3 years. The results are recorded and submitted to BINDT.

Question 22: A failed PCN specific exam can be re-sat:

  • A. Twice within the validity period (typically 1 year), then re-training required
  • B. Once only
  • C. Unlimited
  • D. Never

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: ISO 9712 allows re-examination of failed components twice within the qualifying period. After two failures, re-training is required before another attempt. Practical and theory papers can be re-sat independently.

Question 23: A PCN certificate identifies:

  • A. Method, level, sector, expiry date, and unique certificate number
  • B. Only the candidate name
  • C. Only the employer
  • D. No information

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: PCN certificate clearly states method (UT, RT, MT, PT, ET, VT), level (1, 2, 3), sector (welds, castings, etc.), holder name and ID, issue date, expiry date, and unique certificate number for verification on the BINDT portal.

Question 24: To upgrade from PCN Level 2 to Level 3 requires:

  • A. Additional formal training, accumulated experience as Level 2, and passing the Level 3 Basic + Method exams
  • B. Document review only
  • C. Self-declaration
  • D. Time alone

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: PCN Level 3 (like ASNT Level III) requires Basic exam (cross-method knowledge) and Method exam (depth in one method). Experience after Level 2 (typically 1 to 2 years) is a prerequisite. See our Level 2 vs 3 comparison.

Question 25: A PCN Level 2 inspector’s primary scope of authority is:

  • A. Set up equipment, perform tests per a procedure, interpret indications, write NDT instructions, train Level 1
  • B. Write and approve procedures
  • C. Approve all NDT methods
  • D. Train Level 3

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: ISO 9712 / PCN Level 2 scope: equipment setup, calibration, test execution, indication interpretation, evaluation to acceptance criteria, instruction writing from procedures, training Level 1. Procedure writing and approval is Level 3 only.

Study Tips for PCN Level 2

  • Use a PCN-approved training organization (ATO): Your training must come from a registered ATO for the syllabus and hours to count. BINDT maintains the list at bindt.org.
  • Practice the practical: The practical exam has the highest failure rate. Spend 50+ hours on real specimens before exam day. Practice writing instructions until you can produce a complete one in 30 minutes.
  • Tab the standards: EN ISO 17640 (UT of welds), EN ISO 17636 (RT), EN ISO 5817 (visual quality), EN ISO 23277/23278 (PT/MT acceptance).
  • Closed-book preparation: Unlike ASNT specific (open-book), PCN specific is closed-book. Memorize key acceptance values and parameter limits.
  • Practice 500+ questions: Atlantis prep program delivers 500+ questions across general and specific for each method.

Recommended Study Materials

  • ISO 9712:2021 NDT — Qualification and certification of NDT personnel
  • PCN General Requirements (PCN/GEN) latest edition
  • PCN Method-Specific syllabi (CP-7 UT, CP-8 RT, etc.)
  • EN ISO 5817, 11666, 10675, 23277, 23278 (acceptance standards)
  • EN ISO 17640, 17636, 9712, 9934 (method standards)
  • BINDT NDT Yearbook for industry context
  • Atlantis NDT PCN Level 2 preparation course (in partnership with approved ATO)

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What is the main difference between PCN and ASNT certification?

A: PCN is third-party (BINDT issues the certificate). ASNT (under SNT-TC-1A) is employer-based. ASNT also offers third-party certification (ACCP / ASNT Central Certification). See our full ASNT vs PCN comparison.

Q: Is PCN accepted in the USA?

A: Increasingly yes, especially in oil & gas and offshore. Some US codes (ASME) still default to ASNT, but PCN holders are widely accepted in international and multinational contracts.

Q: How long does the full PCN Level 2 process take?

A: Typically 6 to 12 months: training (1 to 2 weeks), accumulating required experience hours (often during work between training and exam), then 1 to 2 days of exams.

Q: Does PCN expire if I don’t work in NDT for a year?

A: PCN requires continuous practice. Gaps over 12 months may invalidate certification. Always verify with BINDT and your employer.

Q: What is the PCN Level 2 cost?

A: Training fees vary (typically £1,500 to £2,500 per method) plus BINDT exam fees (~£500 to £700 per method). Total cost £2,000 to £3,500 per method.

Q: Does Atlantis NDT offer PCN preparation?

A: Yes — we deliver PCN preparation in partnership with approved ATOs. Our 80-hour blended program covers theory, practical, and mock exams. Call +1 (281) 840-8969 to discuss the next cohort.

Q: Can I hold both PCN and ASNT certifications?

A: Yes, many international inspectors hold both. They are complementary — ASNT for US work and PCN for international.

Q: How does PCN Level 2 in welds relate to CSWIP 3.1?

A: CSWIP 3.1 is a visual welding inspector qualification. PCN Level 2 weld sector is an NDT method qualification (UT, RT, MT, PT) applied to welds. Many inspectors hold both for complete fabrication inspection coverage.

Q: What is the PCN Level 2 pass rate?

A: First-attempt averages 60 to 75%. The practical exam has the highest failure rate. Structured prep raises pass rates to 85%+.

Q: How does PCN compare to API 510/570/653?

A: PCN certifies you in NDT methods. API 510/570/653 certify you as an in-service inspector of vessels, piping, or tanks. Many inspectors hold both PCN (for NDT skill) and API (for in-service inspection role).

About Atlantis NDT

Atlantis NDT is a global NDT technology and services company headquartered in Houston, Texas with operations across India and the Middle East. We deliver accredited NDT training, technical consulting, certification preparation, and digital inspection software trusted by oil & gas, fabrication, EPC, and power generation clients. Our team of ASNT Level III instructors has trained thousands of inspectors worldwide.

Whether you are preparing for ASNT certification, API 510, API 570, or API 653, our exam preparation programs combine classroom theory, hands-on practical training, and proctored mock exams that mirror the real test environment.

Call us at +1 (281) 840-8969 or email sales@atlantisndt.com to enroll in the next training cohort. Same-day quotes for corporate group training in Houston, Dubai, Riyadh, Hyderabad, and on-site at your facility.
